//: Story Phase 4, chapter 15: Morning with the Frog Grog. Starts when the captain sleeps after Phase 3 (the bed in his cabin). Breakfast is in the galley round the long table (7..9,7): Garrick sits at (7,6), Squawks is in his padded basket at (10,7), the captain stands at (8,8). The Dead Center rolls in from the aft bulkhead (galley_breakfast) and the only way out is the ladder (14,3); the crew regroup on deck by the main hatch.

start: Your bed. Feather mattress, red wool blanket, and, very faintly, beard.

p4c1.begin.narrate: The Grand Stenchmaster rowed home from another ocean, as he always does, and the ship has settled into what the crew have started calling the new normal.

p4c1.begin: Mornings aboard the Queen Anne's Revenge come in a fixed order now. First the coughing. Then the gagging. Then the bell. Then the Frog Grog.

p4c1.begin.tutorial: Morning ration is served in the Galley (down the main hatch, midships). Go and get yours.
p4c1.begin.title: Today's Forecast

p4c1.ration: The galley is full, and nobody is enjoying it.
mags: Ration. One each. Don't look at it.
She slides a pewter mug across the table to you.
The Frog Grog has a greasy film on top, a colour that isn't in any rainbow, and something in it that might be a lump.
bob[concerned]: Is it me, or is it getting... older?
gristle[disgusted]: It's got a skin on it. Grog shouldn't have a skin.
garrick[businesslike]: It's developing complexity.
pete[disgusted]: It's developing LUMPS.
A single bubble rises through Bob's mug, very slowly, reaches the top, and pops.
garrick[proud]: There. You see that? A bubble. That's maturity.
bob[sad]: I miss rum. Proper rum. Rum that just sat there in the cup and minded its own business.
brask[disgusted]: Rum that didn't look BACK at you.
You are holding your mug as far from your face as your arm will go. It is not far enough.
wick[concerned]: Still no luck with the beard, Captain?
captain[tired]: Seawater. Soap. Lemons. Vinegar. Sand. Smoke. Herbs.
captain[tired]: I have scrubbed it with everything on this ship that isn't nailed down, and some things that were.
garrick[businesslike]: It won't come out, Captain. I did say. It's bonded. At the molecular beard level.
captain[resigned]: ...I've stopped asking what that means.
garrick[smug]: Very wise.
At the end of the table, Captain Squawks sits in a padded basket, wrapped in his blanket and his little knitted cap. Mags has put a thimble of grog in front of him.
squawks[insulting]: No.
He pushes the thimble away with one foot.
captain[tender]: Wisest decision anyone's made all morning, Squawks.
squawks[smug]: Squawks is WISE.
Across the table, the Grand Stenchmaster is eating his breakfast with enormous dignity.

He is wearing something new: a broad sash, mustard yellow, edged in burgundy and trimmed with something that is trying very hard to be gold. On the chest, somebody has embroidered a nose under a crown. Badly.
captain: ...What is that.
garrick[proud]: The sash of office, Captain. The Grand Stenchmaster's sash.
bob: He made it out of the other curtain.
garrick[offended]: I COMMISSIONED it. From myself. At a very reasonable rate.
garrick[businesslike]: An office needs regalia, Captain. Nobody takes a Grand Stenchmaster seriously in a curtain.
brask: Nobody takes him seriously in the sash either.
garrick[smug]: They will.
Around the table, everyone is waiting for somebody to ask the only question that matters any more.

p4c1.ration.tutorial: Ask Garrick the morning question. (Talk to him.)
p4c1.ration.title: Today's Forecast

p4c1.question: captain: Garrick.
garrick[smug]: Grand Stenchmaster.
captain[determined]: Where is the Dead Center today?
The galley goes silent. Bob stops chewing. Pete puts his spoon down. Even the grog stops bubbling.
These days it's the most important question on the ship. Nobody gets dressed without asking it.
pete[worried]: The normal stink, you can live in. It's horrible. You breathe through your mouth and think about something else.
gristle[concerned]: The Center's different. The Center's the thick part. The yellow part. Warm, like standing too near the stove.
bob[concerned]: Five breaths of that and you're on the floor. Doc says three, for Wick.
garrick[businesslike]: It's the heart of the original event, Captain. The concentrated core of my treasure-room... contribution. The part that never thinned out. And it wanders.
garrick[proud]: The part that still remembers coming out.
brask[disgusted]: We ASKED you not to call it that.
wick[disgusted]: Everybody asked him not to call it that.
garrick[businesslike]: Which is why, as of this morning, the Grand Stenchmaster's office is proud to present...
garrick[delighted]: ...the first official GRAND STENCHMASTER STENCH FORECAST!
He unrolls a sheet of paper across the table, on top of your breakfast, and weighs it down with the grog.
pete[tired]: The fart forecast.
garrick[offended]: The STENCH forecast.

p4c1.question.tutorial: Inspect the forecast on the breakfast table.
p4c1.question.title: Today's Forecast

p4c1.forecast.caption: The first Grand Stenchmaster Stench Forecast.

p4c1.forecast: It has been drawn in crayon.
captain[disgusted]: You drew this with CRAYONS.
garrick[offended]: PROFESSIONAL crayons.
captain: There's a duck on the box.
garrick[businesslike]: A professional duck.
captain: What are all the arrows?
garrick[businesslike]: Wind. Probable drift. Possible drift. That one's a correction of that one. That one's decorative.
captain: They point in every direction.
garrick[proud]: So does the Center, Captain. It's a very accurate forecast.
captain: And this... thing. In the corner.
garrick: Garlic.
captain: It has legs.
garrick[businesslike]: Weather symbol. Don't worry about it.

garrick[businesslike]: My professional reading: forty percent chance of the Center around the galley. Sixty percent around the cannon deck by midday. Possible occupation of the sleeping quarters later.
brask: That's a hundred percent already. And then some.
garrick[smug]: The Center is very busy.
captain: And across the bottom it says 'bad here'. And under that, 'probably'.
garrick[businesslike]: Forecasting is an art as well as a science.
captain[concerned]: And this enormous yellow scribble? Here? Right behind the table?
captain[concerned]: Right behind where we're all sitting?
garrick[businesslike]: Ah. Yes. That's...
garrick[neutral]: ...hm.
garrick[surprised]: That might be now.
Nobody moves.
Along the aft bulkhead, something thick and yellow is sliding in through the seams. Slowly. Warmly. It has the texture of soup.
captain[alarmed]: SQUAWKS!
You scoop him up, basket, blanket, cap and all, and tuck him under your arm. Your other hand, for some reason, is still holding the grog.

p4c1.forecast.text: Not the hatch, it came FROM there!

p4c1.forecast: The crew scatter. Only the Grand Stenchmaster stays where he is, seated, finishing his toast.
garrick[neutral]: Yes.
garrick[businesslike]: That is the Dead Center.
captain[angry]: Your map said 'MIGHT BE NOW'!
garrick[businesslike]: Forecasts change, Captain.
captain[angry]: It's been a forecast for FOUR SECONDS!
garrick[smug]: And look how much it's changed already.

p4c1.forecast.tutorial: Get out! Up the ladder in the corner (top right), before the Center reaches you. Watch the FUMES meter.
p4c1.forecast.title: Clear the Breakfast Area

p4c1.no_door: You'd have to go through the Center to get to that door.
p4c1.no_hatch: Down there is the hold, and past the hold is the treasure room. That's where it came from.
captain: Up. Not down. Never down.
p4c1.regroup: You come up out of the hatch into the daylight, coughing, and set Squawks down on the deck.
squawks[worried]: Breakfast gone?
captain[tired]: Breakfast gone.
bob[sad]: My breakfast. I'd had two bites. It was the good biscuit, Captain. The one without the weevil.
bob[concerned]: I could run down and get it. Quick. Hold my breath.
The Grand Stenchmaster climbs out of the hatch behind you, at his leisure, dabbing his mouth with a napkin.
garrick[businesslike]: I wouldn't, Mister Bob. It's been in the Center. Your breakfast belongs to the Center now.
bob[sad]: ...Can I have it back later?
garrick[businesslike]: Oh, you can have it back. You won't want it.
captain[angry]: Garrick. Your forecast. The one you made TWO MINUTES AGO.
garrick[businesslike]: Ah. Yes.
He studies it for a moment, nods to himself, and crumples it into a ball.
garrick[businesslike]: Obsolete.
He tosses it over his shoulder without looking.
It drops, very neatly, into the mug of Frog Grog you have somehow carried all the way up the ladder.
You stare at it.
garrick[proud]: Recycling.
captain[angry]: That was my RATION.
garrick[delighted]: And now it's fortified! Added fibre!
captain[angry]: Go away.
garrick[businesslike]: Of course, Captain. Straight after the announcement.
garrick[proud]: Ladies and gentlemen of the Queen Anne's Revenge! From today, a fresh forecast will be posted every morning at the Grand Stenchmaster's station!
Next to his barrel there is a new board, with a crayon cloud painted on it and a sign that says FORECAST.
garrick[proud]: The Forecast Board! Today's forecast, and every forecast I've ever made, for reference.
pete[tired]: Is it going to be right?
garrick[smug]: It's going to be POSTED.

p4c1.regroup.tutorial: The Forecast Board at Garrick's station keeps every forecast he makes. Take a look. (The forecasts are also in your pause menu from now on.)
p4c1.regroup.title: Today's Forecast

p4c1.board_first: captain[tired]: 'Result: wrong almost immediately.' He wrote that himself.
garrick[proud]: Honesty is the foundation of any forecasting operation, Captain.
garrick[businesslike]: New one every morning. Ring four bells if you see me drawing. It helps people prepare.
